SDE internship: remote software engineering in 4 weeks

An SDE internship is a software development engineer internship: you design, write, test and ship code. SkillMe's remote SDE internship runs 4 weeks. You build ShelfSpace, a layered backend service with data structures, a REST API, caching, tests and CI, one reviewed milestone a week. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

The Software Engineering (SDE) internship in short

In the SkillMe Software Engineering (SDE) internship you build ShelfSpace: Library Lending Service, a project where you build a small layered backend service for tracking books and loans, with real automated tests and applied data-structure work baked into actual features. In week 1 you design the core data model for a library lending service and implement it as clean, layered Python code with an in-memory store, before touching a database or API. By week 4 you add automated CI, handle a batch-import feature efficiently using an appropriate data structure for deduplication, and get the service into a state you could actually hand off or deploy. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

Week by week

What each week of the Software Engineering (SDE) internship covers

The four milestones of ShelfSpace: Library Lending Service.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Core Domain Model and In-Memory Service

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Design the core data model for a library lending service and implement it as clean, layered Python code with an in-memory store, before touching a database or API. Getting the domain logic right first makes everything later easier to test and extend.

    What you learn

    • Separating domain models from storage and application logic
    • Designing classes for a small real-world domain (books, copies, loans)
    • Writing a service layer that enforces business rules
    • Basic unit testing with pytest

    What you submit

    • models.py with Book, Copy and Loan dataclasses
    • In-memory BookRepository and LoanRepository
    • A LibraryService enforcing checkout/return business rules with custom exceptions
    • A pytest suite covering happy paths and error paths
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • pytest -v runs and all tests pass with no warnings
    • Checking out the last available copy of a book then attempting one more raises NoCopyAvailableError
    • Returning a loan twice raises a clear error instead of silently succeeding or crashing
    • The domain logic in library_service.py has no direct dependency on any storage implementation detail beyond calling the repository interface

    Stretch goal: Add a LibraryService.list_overdue(today) method that returns all loans past their due date, with a test using a fixed fake 'today' date.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Search, Ranking and a REST API

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Expose last week's service as a real HTTP API, and add a search feature with relevance ranking — an applied use of sorting and string-matching data structures inside a real feature, not an isolated algorithm exercise.

    What you learn

    • Building a REST API with FastAPI (or Flask) over an existing service layer
    • Implementing simple relevance-ranked search using string matching and scoring
    • Using a sort with a custom key function to rank results
    • Writing API-level tests with a test client, separate from unit tests

    What you submit

    • A REST API exposing checkout, return, book listing and loan lookup
    • Proper HTTP status code mapping from service exceptions
    • A scored, ranked search_books feature with a search endpoint
    • API-level tests using a test client, separate from Week 1's unit tests
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • GET /books/search?q=<word> returns results ordered with exact title matches before partial matches
    • Attempting to check out a book with zero available copies returns HTTP 409, not a 500 error
    • Looking up a nonexistent loan ID returns HTTP 404 with a clear error body
    • All API tests pass and are clearly separate (by file or folder) from Week 1's unit tests

    Stretch goal: Add pagination to GET /books (?page=1&page_size=10) and a test confirming page boundaries are correct.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Persistence, Caching and Concurrency Safety

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Swap the in-memory store for a real SQLite database, and add a small LRU-style in-memory cache for repeated lookups — applying a hash-map-backed cache data structure inside a real performance feature, plus handling concurrent checkout attempts safely.

    What you learn

    • Persisting a domain model to SQLite with sqlite3 or a lightweight ORM
    • Implementing a simple LRU cache using a dict plus an ordered structure
    • Handling a race condition: two near-simultaneous checkouts for the last copy
    • Writing integration tests against a real (temporary) database

    What you submit

    • SQLite-backed repositories implementing the same interface as the in-memory ones
    • A hand-implemented LRUCache used for search result caching with invalidation
    • A concurrency safeguard preventing double-checkout of the last available copy
    • Integration tests running against a real temporary SQLite database
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • Switching the config flag from in-memory to SQLite requires no changes to LibraryService code
    • A test proves the search cache is hit on a repeated identical query (fewer underlying DB calls on the second call)
    • A test simulating two concurrent checkouts for the last copy results in exactly one success and one clear failure, never both succeeding
    • Integration tests pass against a real temporary SQLite file and clean up after themselves

    Stretch goal: Add a cache hit/miss counter exposed at GET /stats so you can observe cache effectiveness while using the API.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    CI, Load Handling and Deployment Readiness

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Add automated CI, handle a batch-import feature efficiently using an appropriate data structure for deduplication, and get the service into a state you could actually hand off or deploy. This week is the engineering polish that makes the project real, not just working on your machine.

    What you learn

    • Setting up continuous integration to run the full test suite automatically
    • Efficient batch processing using a set for deduplication instead of repeated linear scans
    • Basic structured logging and a health-check endpoint
    • Packaging a service for deployment (environment config, requirements.txt, run instructions)

    What you submit

    • A working GitHub Actions CI workflow running the full test suite on push
    • A bulk POST /books/import endpoint using set-based deduplication
    • Structured request logging middleware and a GET /health endpoint
    • A DEPLOY.md and a clean, pinned dependency file
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • Pushing a commit triggers CI and the full test suite passes in the Actions log
    • Importing 500+ books with duplicate ISBNs adds each unique book exactly once and reports the correct skipped count
    • GET /health correctly reports a healthy status when the DB is reachable
    • A fresh clone of the repo can install dependencies and pass pytest using only DEPLOY.md and the README

    Stretch goal: Add a rate limit on /checkout (e.g. max 10 requests per IP per minute) using a simple in-memory token bucket, with a test confirming the 11th rapid request is rejected.

Is it for you?

Software Engineering (SDE) internship: questions and answers

What is an SDE internship?

SDE stands for Software Development Engineer. An SDE internship is a software engineering internship where you build and test real code. In this one you build a backend service over four weeks: a domain model, search and a REST API, persistence with caching and concurrency safety, then CI and deployment readiness.

What does SDE intern mean?

An SDE intern is a Software Development Engineer intern: a student or graduate doing software engineering work for a fixed period. The title is common at product companies; the work is writing, testing and shipping code.

Is this SDE internship remote?

Yes. It is a remote SDE internship open to students in any country, at about 2–3 hours a week.

What will I build in the Software Engineering (SDE) internship?

You build ShelfSpace: Library Lending Service. Build a small layered backend service for tracking books and loans, with real automated tests and applied data-structure work baked into actual features. It is one project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the Software Engineering (SDE) internship?

The Software Engineering (SDE) internship works with Data Structures, System Design and Testing. Week 1: separating domain models from storage and application logic; designing classes for a small real-world domain (books, copies, loans). Week 2: building a REST API with FastAPI (or Flask) over an existing service layer; implementing simple relevance-ranked search using string matching and scoring. Week 3: persisting a domain model to SQLite with sqlite3 or a lightweight ORM; implementing a simple LRU cache using a dict plus an ordered structure. Week 4: setting up continuous integration to run the full test suite automatically; efficient batch processing using a set for deduplication instead of repeated linear scans.

Do I need experience to apply for the Software Engineering (SDE) internship?

You need the basics of Data Structures, System Design and Testing, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you design the core data model for a library lending service and implement it as clean, layered Python code with an in-memory store, before touching a database or API. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each Software Engineering (SDE) milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of ShelfSpace: Library Lending Service, that means: pytest -v runs and all tests pass with no warnings; checking out the last available copy of a book then attempting one more raises NoCopyAvailableError; returning a loan twice raises a clear error instead of silently succeeding or crashing; the domain logic in library_service.py has no direct dependency on any storage implementation detail beyond calling the repository interface. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the Software Engineering (SDE) internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Designed a layered library service with domain models, repositories and business logic cleanly separated; Wrote a pytest suite covering both happy paths and real error conditions; Learned to keep business rules out of the storage layer for easier testing and future changes; Built a REST API over a layered service, mapping domain errors to correct HTTP status codes; Implemented ranked search with a custom scoring function and sort key; Wrote API-level tests with a test client separate from my unit test suite; Swapped an in-memory repository for SQLite persistence without changing any service-layer code; Implemented a hand-written LRU cache for search results with proper invalidation; Fixed a real race condition allowing double-checkout of the last available copy; Set up CI so every push automatically runs the full backend test suite; Used a set for O(1) deduplication in a bulk import handling 500+ records efficiently; Got a small backend service to a real deploy-ready state with health checks and docs.

Is the Software Engineering (SDE) internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based: 8–10 interns are picked each month from those who complete the internship and hold an issued certificate. It is not paid to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
